units.characteristics: the interior fleeing its calling / the presence of God
units.gist: NARRATIVE - the call to Nineveh; 'but Jonah rose to FLEE to Tarshish from the PRESENCE OF THE LORD' (twice) - the self running from its commission and from God's face; the downward drift (down to Joppa, down into the ship, down to sleep)

units.characteristics: the sleeping prophet vs the praying pagans; the responsive outsiders
units.gist: the storm; Jonah asleep in the hold while the pagan sailors cry each to his god; 'I fear the LORD... who made the sea'; thrown overboard, the sea stills; 'the men FEARED THE LORD exceedingly' - the outsiders more responsive to God than the fleeing prophet

units.characteristics: the drowning self's cry and thanksgiving; salvation belongs to the LORD
units.gist: from the belly: 'out of my distress I called... out of the belly of Sheol I cried, and you heard'; 'when my life was fainting away, I REMEMBERED the LORD'; 'those who pay regard to vain idols forsake their hope of steadfast love'; 'SALVATION BELONGS TO THE LORD'

units.characteristics: the pagan city's repentance; God relenting
units.gist: the second call; 'the people of Nineveh BELIEVED GOD', fasted, the king rose from his throne to sackcloth; 'who knows? God may relent'; 'let everyone TURN from his evil way'; 'God saw... how they turned, and God RELENTED' - genuine repentance answered by mercy

units.characteristics: the resentment of grace shown to enemies
units.gist: GEM - 'it displeased Jonah exceedingly, and he was ANGRY'; 'I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, relenting from disaster - THAT is why I fled'; 'better for me to die than to live' - the heart that resents God's mercy to enemies

units.characteristics: the narrow heart vs the divine compassion
units.gist: GEM - the plant, the worm, the scorching wind; Jonah's pity for the plant he did not make; God's question: 'you PITY the plant... and should not I PITY Nineveh, that great city' - the self's misplaced pity exposed against God's vast compassion; the book ends on God's question
